items.abstract: <jats:p>As the building industry moves toward sustainability and intelligent structures, there&apos;s been an increased demand for integrated energy management solutions that synchronize renewable energy systems, HVAC systems, and smart electrical networks. Studies of these subsystems are often conducted separately, however, and there is limited research investigated in an integrated framework to explain how these subsystems work together in building energy systems.,This study reviews the latest advancements in integration of renewable energy, HVAC optimization, and smart electrical network management in buildings, from a structured literature review and a systems-integration approach. Dominant technologies, operational coordination methods, optimization methods, and sustainability aspects of intelligent building energy systems were identified by analyzing relevant peer-reviewed literature.,The concept of ML-IBEMF is proposed and introduced in this paper, which aims to integrate renewable energy generation systems, HVAC optimization mechanism, smart electrical coordination and digital intelligence technologies into a unified analytical framework, connecting to sustainability performance outcomes. The research also advances the theory of intelligent buildings, sustainable energy and sustainable building design and offers practical design and management recommendations for those using intelligent building energy systems.</jats:p>
